items.title: 68357_Jimmy Maxwell oral history interview
items.q: So I used to play with the kids and picked up a little bit of the language. ... Ijiro was first son.

ctx.x: You mentioned that you studied Japanese. When did you take that up, Jimmy?

Well again, back to California. It's kind of a retroactive story. California had race laws against the Japanese. Japanese people could not own property, immigrants. So what they'd do, they'd get some friendly Caucasian to own the farm until their oldest son became of age and then they would buy it back in his name.

My grandfather owned a farm for this Takota family that lived next to us until Hijir --- Ijiro became of age. Ijiro was first son. Then he sold it to them for $1.00. So I used to play with the kids and picked up a little bit of the language. Then in 1936, in Los Angeles, I became very interested in Zen Buddhism and I met the Zen master from Japan and I learned more Japanese from him.
